approach.method_basis: The Parent searches with two molecular regions, each owning its accepted descendants, local count-fingerprint Gaussian-process model, center and bounded graph-edit neighborhood. The regions compete for oracle purchases through posterior draws in score units, using a shared response amplitude estimated from the session accepted archive. Purchased improvements over each region own center expand its neighborhood; repeated failures contract it and eventually restart it at an already scored root with a singleton model. A region with no purchases leaves its progress counters unchanged.
approach.novelty: Change the progress reference to the best accepted score in the whole session, frozen before the batch. A locally improving region will stop receiving success credit when its new purchases do not sufficiently beat that shared reference. This can let persistent global underperformance trigger contraction or restart sooner. Earlier siblings changed restart training context or root separation; this changes only the success information consumed by the existing controller, keeping owned-only models and the original root rule.

observed_bottleneck: Complete code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce can reset a region failure counter after local recovery that does not sufficiently improve the session incumbent. Independent reconstruction of its 15 frozen Search cells verifies 870 transitions: 523 paid and 347 no-purchase, 209 local successes versus 196 prebatch-global successes. All 13 disagreements change the one-step counter state; two also change radius or retirement, and four occur after restart. This is exposed decision evidence, not a counterfactual adaptive score. All 19 actual Parent resets already received immediate feedback, so blanket reset starvation is contradicted. Parent global increment mass is 5.641824681825608/4350 overall and 0.8322070529143053/2175 in the final half of optimizer receipts; post-reset mass is only 0.11690985499057077/950. Parent mean is 0.58461375649735, population SD 0.01681763193120207, versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de mean 0.607030316211131. The separated-root sibling n-7c404cb14467 shows large observed local recovery with little global gain, and context sibling n-f3e58c614c9d changes fitting and purchases; both lack complete seed-1 endpoints and neither supplies a full-panel benefit or refutation. hypothesis: On code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce, replace only the success reference of the existing purchased-progress controller. Freeze G=max(score of every unique already accepted current-session archive record) before each announcement. For each region r with at least one actual accepted owned purchase in that batch, success_r is exactly max(new owned scores_r) > G + tolerance_relative*max(abs(G),tolerance_score_floor). Both regions use the identical frozen G, even when both beat it or when observe processes one region earlier. With zero accepted owned purchases success remains null and no progress counter changes. The existing success/failure, expansion, contraction and retirement law consumes that boolean unchanged. The regional center still advances to the best owned episode record even when such a local gain is classified as global failure. This separates local search position from global progress credit; rejecting local-only success should expose sustained global failure to the existing contraction/restart mechanism and may improve subsequent purchased global gain.

finding_summary.headline: Global progress control changed restarts and raised gain rates, but missed its endpoint target.
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out a wiring or feedback-exposure explanation for this adjustment: the shared reference, exact arithmetic, ownership and unchanged local-center updates all check out, and all new episodes receive purchases. Its influence is narrow: only four complete molecule-and-score trajectories differ, all in two tasks, while the other eleven remain identical. More resets still convert poorly into global progress: 1,188 post-reset purchases yield only 0.190517 of the total 5.664501 global increment mass, although that rate improves over the Parent. Global gain-bearing receipts actually fall from 260 to 255, and the ten largest increments are identical, so the benefit comes from a limited redistribution of later progress rather than broad improvement throughout search. Molecular evidence shows continued refinement of related aromatic/carbonyl or fluorinated heterocyclic families, fewer typed/generic scaffolds (1,858/1,215 versus 1,880/1,234), and slightly larger fragment and oversized tails. Ring diversity alone therefore has not delivered consistently useful alternative frameworks. A proposal operator that preserves functional architecture while changing ring/linker frameworks, or a restart search scheme that reaches different useful basins, addresses that method limitation more directly than this progress-reference change. Those are method diagnoses, not tested improvements; these records do not establish a surrogate-ranking fault or show that removing unusual bonds improves scores. The borrowed global-utility rule worked in its scalar, frozen-batch adaptation, but this result does not validate the other MORBO components. What is settled is the registered adjustment’s subthreshold finite-panel benefit; useful regional search under a different substantive intervention remains open.
finding_summary.results: The global-reference controller executed correctly in all 15 task/seed runs. Across 535 paid regional updates, eight updates that would have counted as local successes became global failures; all eight changed counter state, and two immediately changed contraction or retirement. All 335 updates without a purchase preserved their state. Actual restarts rose from 19 to 24 and every restart immediately received feedback. Full global increment mass rose from 5.641825 to 5.664501 over 4,350 purchases, and late mass rose from 0.832207 to 0.860209 over 2,175 purchases, so both registered gain rates improved. The complete mean endpoint rose from 0.584614 to 0.586125, a gain of 0.001512 with population SD 0.016666, below the required 0.002. Seed gains were 0, 0.002533 and 0.002003. Twelve of fifteen endpoints were unchanged; median_2 gained 0.012663 in one seed and lost 0.016531 in another, while sitagliptin_mpo gained 0.026545 in one seed. The mean remains 0.020905 below the formal Anchor. Thus execution and the predicted controller behavior are supported, but the registered conjunction of better gain rates and at least 0.002 endpoint gain is refuted by its endpoint limb. This is a small measured improvement that misses its declared usefulness target, not a technical failure or an absence of activation.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with N-halogen liabilities, unresolved stereochemistry and wider size extremes.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-970847a1987c produces ring-rich aromatic and heteroaromatic molecules, including carbonyl/nitrile compounds, basic amine-bearing saturated rings, linked aza-aromatics, imide-like cores and unusual expanded or densely fused polycycles. The digest and every listed Child and published code-Parent trajectory were read: both child_complete and paired_complete are true for frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 against n-7d1e6230ecce; no requested path or paired cell is missing. Each node has 4,350 evaluated optimizer records, 870 per task. Descriptor populations exclude initial records, which were read separately; these are accepted output molecules, not all unpurchased candidate fields or rejected attempts. All audited optimizer SMILES parse. Child ring-containing/aromatic-containing counts are 4,184/4,139, consistent with the digest's high text-level rates. The chemical repertoire has rings and ionizable amine motifs; their absence is not the limitation. The principal gaps are conventional bond connectivity, preservation of complete bounded-size architecture, explicit stereochemical identity and chemically interpretable framework exploration. Synthetic plausibility is questionable overall, despite familiar medicinal fragments. The Child has 1,008 N-halogen-containing and 104 O-halogen-containing records versus Parent 1,017 and 104. It has 148 records below six heavy atoms and 255 above fifty versus Parent 134 and 245. Potential tetrahedral centers are found in 2,302 Child records, with none assigned; the digest also has zero stereocentre-text rate for every task. Current same-method Parent remeasurement gives 2,114 records with potential centers and none assigned; this uses RDKit 2023.09.6 FindMolChiralCenters with includeUnassigned=True and useLegacyImplementation=False, and is not an inherited older count. Neutral/uncharged SMILES do not imply an absence of basic amines, and unspecified stereo is not proof of a scoring opportunity. Global typed/generic nonempty Murcko scaffolds are 1,858/1,215 versus Parent 1,880/1,234; this is graph diversity, not demonstrated synthetic or useful diversity. The first three tasks retain identical ordered molecule-and-score trajectories. Twelve of the fifteen endpoint structures/scores are unchanged; endpoint differences occur in the remaining families, with mixed chemical changes. An endpoint means the highest observed score, not the last evaluated proposal. No separate formal-Anchor molecular comparison was performed; that comparison is absent rather than inferred from the code Parent. This report makes no activation, selection, causal-component or practical synthesis/pharmacology claim. All judgments and transferable gaps retain their origin in this frozen Search output; older Parent gaps are not reassigned to the intervention. Evidence provenance: policy/requests/r0053-03-improve-L01-molecular-assess-e1c506bb69cda8a4.json; policy/scratch/r0053-03-improve-L01-molecular/trajectory_manifest.json; policy/scratch/r0053-03-improve-L01-molecular/chemistry_summary.json. The read historical baseline report is nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/molecular.json, but numerical comparisons above were independently recomputed from its published trajectories. Each task cites its audits and underlying files. In-run Child snapshots preserve the exact trusted staging bytes and original paths/hashes without inventing future archive paths.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-970847a1987c, frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, evaluated optimizer output only: 1,008 of 4,350 structures carry direct N-halogen bonds and 104 carry O-halogen bonds. The paired published n-7d1e6230ecce population has 1,017 and 104. Strong observed structures include a three-N-F framework and an N-brominated amide, so this is a repeated chemical-quality limitation, not a demonstrated penalty in the scores or attribution to the changed component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently elaborate conventional bond connectivity while retaining otherwise recognizable aromatic and carbonyl architectures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic capability would offer conventional bond/substituent alternatives while preserving a molecule's observed size, heteroatom arrangement and attachment geometry. Their usefulness must be learned from accepted feedback in the current session; these observations do not justify forcing a target motif or assuming that deleting N-halogen bonds raises a score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-970847a1987c under the same frozen Search and accepted-output conditions: 148 optimizer structures have fewer than six heavy atoms and 255 exceed fifty, compared with 134 and 245 in paired n-7d1e6230ecce. Observed low-score examples include isolated fragments and very large recombinations, whereas several upper-score examples retain medium-sized connected aromatic/carbonyl or amine/aromatic frameworks. These are measured output associations; no size law or component mediation is established.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve complete molecular architecture while varying size and substituents.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need scaffold and substituent transformations that can preserve functional connectivity without routinely severing a useful architecture or duplicating whole ring blocks. Use current-session observations to discover where size changes help; the descriptive tail boundaries are not a prescribed universal atom-count cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-970847a1987c, frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2: the digest reports zero stereocentre-text rate throughout, and the stated RDKit audit finds potential tetrahedral centers in 2,302 of 4,350 optimizer records with no assigned tetrahedral centers. The paired Parent also has no assignments. Substituted saturated rings and benzylic linkers among the cited upper-score structures expose this representational gap, without establishing a scoring benefit from resolving it.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves potential stereochemical identities unresolved in the structures it actually evaluates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Concrete chemical output would need consistent representation and retention of stereochemical identity through graph edits. Any later task-agnostic investigation must use actual session feedback to test whether distinguishing those identities matters; the present evidence supports a representation limitation, not a pharmacological or optimization claim.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-970847a1987c and paired n-7d1e6230ecce in the same frozen Search panel: typed/generic nonempty scaffold totals are 1,858/1,215 and 1,880/1,234. Upper-score series repeatedly retain related aromatic carbonyl, fluorinated heterocyclic or amine-bearing cores, sometimes with unusual expanded or densely fused ring topology. Changed endpoint frameworks accompany both higher and lower observed scores. This retains the earlier Parent limitation as conditional output evidence, not proof that the current intervention caused it.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring rewrites do not yet establish reliable access to chemically interpretable alternative frameworks with useful scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic capability would preserve useful functional arrangements while proposing coherent alternative ring and linker frameworks, with structural interpretability assessed separately from novelty. Actual accepted feedback must establish useful diversity; unique scaffolds, added rings or lower endpoint similarity alone do not establish improvement.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
